subject: Orion Health dedicated pool orchestration — sprint brief & questions
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Orion Health dedicated pool onboarding — reqs + first pass

Hi Alex / Soojin,

Kicking off the implementation handshake for Orion Health (deal 3489). Customer is ready to move from pilot to reserved pool and wants a predictable regional footprint for EU first with US fallback. I attached a brief with their traffic profile and the near-term SOW draft. High-level asks from CS and the customer: 

- Dedicated GPU pool (initially 8 x A100 equivalents) scoped for steady-state inference.
- Autoscale policy: scale to 24 GPUs on sustained load; burst to 40 for short spikes (matched to our burst pricing tiers).
- Multi-region routing: primary eu-central, fallback us-west for overflow.
- KV/prefix caching for repeated clinical templates (latency SLO 150ms median).
- SOC2 evidence and IP allowlisting before any private endpoints are enabled.

Immediate questions we need answered to finalize the pool config:
1) Expected QPS / peak token throughput and typical generation lengths (see attached traffic_profile.csv)
2) Any special quantization/profile requirements for their model variants?
3) Compliance gating timeline for on-prem-like access policies.

Customer contacts: Anna Li (Engineering lead) and Samir Patel (Infrastructure) copied on this thread.

Can you take the lead on config proposals? Suggest we do a canary window of 48 hours after handover and a staged rollback plan.

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Attachments: orion_requirements.xlsx, SOW_v0.9.pdf
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Health dedicated pool onboarding — reqs + first pass

Thanks Monica — reviewing. Quick run of clarifying asks so ops can size things correctly: 

- Token-level throughput: can Anna confirm expected peak tokens/sec per model variant? The CSV shows bursts but I want steady-state numbers for autoscale thresholds.
- Sequence length: are they sending variable-length prompts up to 2048 tokens or capped shorter? This affects KV cache sizing.
- Model flavor: are they planning to run a single LLM (open-34B-quant) or multiple variants that require model routing?

Proposed initial pool config (draft):
- Pool: orion-eu-dedicated-1 — 8 GPUs (baseline) / autoscale min 8 / target 24 / hard cap 40
- Warm-up: maintain 2 hot instances in eu-central to keep initial latency in SLO
- Burst policy: allow burst to 40 for 15-minute windows, with cool-down 30m and cost alerting enabled
- Routing: primary eu-central, overflow to us-west with model pinning to quantized variant in fallback

I'll put a stub runbook together and drop it in the implementation folder. Need Anna's QPS and whether they can tolerate short 5–10 minute throttled windows during canary.

If everyone agrees, I'll schedule an ops-change kickoff for Monday 8/17 to align netops and infra.

—Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.com
From: Anna Li <anna@orionhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T02:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Health dedicated pool onboarding — reqs + first pass

Thanks team — confirming details from Orion Engineering: 

- Expected steady-state: ~120 requests/minute with average generations of ~350 tokens; peaks up to ~520 req/min during end-of-day batch ops. This maps to roughly 700–900 tokens/sec at peak depending on prompt mix.
- Sequence lengths: most requests are 256–512 tokens, but a small fraction (5%) go up to ~1,600 tokens for long-form generation.
- Model variants: we will run two variants — core-gen (quantized 13B) for most inference and a fallback larger variant (34B) for higher-quality responses. We prefer quantized variants in fallback to lower cost.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence can be provided by EOD Friday (8/20). We do require allowlisting of 3 static IPs for our netops team before private endpoints are enabled.

We can tolerate a short 5–10 minute throttling during canary provided we get proactive notices to our SREs. Canary window of 48 hours sounds fine.

I'll upload a slightly more detailed traffic matrix to the HubSpot deal.

—Anna
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@orionhealth.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Health dedicated pool onboarding — reqs + first pass

Great — thanks Anna. Based on the numbers, proposed adjustments: 

- Baseline pool: keep baseline at 8 GPUs but provision heavier memory footprints (for 1,600-token tails) — allocate 20% of baseline for high-memory instances.
- Autoscale thresholds: scale up at sustained 550 tokens/sec for 2 minutes; scale out to 24 at 900 tokens/sec sustained; hard cap at 40 as Alex suggested.
- Burst policy: allow burst of +50% capacity for 15 minutes, but require manual approval for more than 2 consecutive bursts in a 24h window (billing/commit trigger).
- Canary plan: 48h canary starting 2026-08-20 02:00 UTC. During canary we will route 10% of production traffic initially, ramp 10% every 6 hours to 50% then evaluate SLA metrics before full cutover.

Action items for this thread: 
1) Alex: finalize ops runbook (pool naming, autoscale knobs, alert thresholds) — due 2026-08-18 EOD
2) Monica: confirm SOC2 artifacts ETA with customer and collect allowlist IPs — due 2026-08-19
3) Ben: coordinate netops for cross-region failover and pre-create us-west fallback pool config — due 2026-08-19
4) Anna / Orion: upload traffic matrix and confirm allowlist IPs — due 2026-08-19

I'll open a formal implementation epic and attach the runbook draft; linking the HubSpot deal and DocuSign envelope once SOW is signed.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

Looping in netops checklist and a short preflight note: 

Preflight checklist highlights (netops):
- Pre-create us-west fallback pool with quantized 13B routing rules and test model pins
- Ensure cross-region failover health checks run every 30s with a 90s fail threshold
- Add allowlist IPs once Anna provides them; do not enable private endpoints until we have SOC2 evidence in our vault
- Configure cost alerts at 60% of burst budget and an automatic pause scheduler for continuous >6h over-burst behavior

I'll stand up the fallback pool in staging tomorrow and run an internal pressure test against the traffic_profile.csv to validate burst behavior. Will report results in this thread.

—Ben
